Three prior sessions left `plan/F-0067` empty — no `docs/plans/f-0067.md`, no `docs/reviews/1-f-0067.md`, no Task cards anywhere in the repo's history. This was a starved plan, not a content dispute: there were no two readings to weigh, only nothing committed after three attempts. I read the approved spec in full and verified every precondition its §1.1 states against this checkout (`step_health.run()`'s statement order, `worktrees.safety`'s two `unpushed commit(s)` exits, `retention.owned_patterns`, `doctor.run`'s row order, `groom`'s `EXTRA_SECTIONS`, `plugin_build`'s skill list) — all matched exactly, so the spec itself was never the obstacle. `docs/plans/f-0066.md` (landed since, at `eac200f76`) gave the precedent for how this factory plans a tightly-coupled single-new-module feature, and `T-0317`'s ruling (`111165f56`) gave the precedent for not forcing a split where one does not exist. So I wrote and landed the missing plan myself rather than ordering a fourth attempt: five Tasks — `conventions.py`'s `floor:` map (no dependency), the whole of `asf/floor.py` plus its two satellite files `retention.py`/`worktrees.py` (one Task: the registry, probes, sweep and hold branch all share one new file and one test module, and `CLASSES`' own `FloorError` check at import means a partial table fails its own registry test — it does not split), then three independent callers (doctor row, groom section, tick+CLI wiring) that each need only the leaf. One standing, already-repeatedly-recorded defect noted in the plan itself (PD8) and not fixed here, out of this Feature's footprint: `plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE` is four digits and the spec's Story ids are five, so the minted Task cards' `stories:` field will read empty — the same defect a dozen other landed plans in this repo have already recorded at this head. Nothing else was in dispute; the card's own "fold into the clean-floor Feature?" question was already answered by the spec itself (§1.3: stands alone either way) and is not reopened.
